Strategic Scenario Response Proposal—Safe Harbor  

Scenario: Loss of a hospitable Tyria.  

Response Op Designation: Safe Harbor  

Removal of the Wizard's Tower (and perhaps some bastions) from Tyria to a predetermined location in the Mists or a pocket dimension in the event of a world-ending or altering event.  

Primary risk factor(s): A jump into Mists space would be fraught with uncertainties, given its chaotic nature. Acceptable locations would have to be scouted. Perhaps the Bastion of the Obscure could construct some kind of homing signal we could lock onto for the jump?  

Comment: Not impossible. It would require abandoning the World Spire and the beacon network for a time, if they survive. I'd like to hear more about potential return contingencies for this sort of scenario. —Akeem

strings.en:
Project Omega: Post-Mortem  
by Head Researcher Skala  
  
Director Kuda has taken full control over all Inquest operations in Eternity's Garden after former Director Vloxx supposedly turned against the Inquest during his operation at the Spire of Exaltation to the north of our position. Given the fluidity of the current situation, I am writing this report to serve both as my final report on Project Omega as well as my official letter of resignation from the Inquest, effective immediately.  
  
**Conclusions**  
Project Omega was, by the reckoning of our speculated project outcomes, a resounding success. Our three surviving subjects attained powers and abilities far beyond that of an ordinary asura. Yet, the project has been rife with red flags. From shoddy quality control and wasted time on redundant analyses to unclear objectives and goal setting from leadership across the board, Project Omega has been nothing short of a researcher's nightmare.  
  
Director Kuda may not be pleased with these findings, but even she cannot deny that her three "champions" were neither well-suited nor even-tempered enough to handle the levels of power that they have been given.  
  
Whoever finds this, give my regards to the director, but remind her that Skala is nobody's "underling."  
  
I do not expect anyone will find me.

Earned through the Old Lion's Court raid encounter.

While I rarely leave the confines of my domain, I possess the finest and most robust collection of trinkets from around the world. Adventurers travel across Tyria, finding items of all sorts from locations multifarious, and toss them into my forge in the hopes of receiving something better in return.

Most of the time, the skritt handle the method of compensation. I have to imagine that's working out just fine, considering I've yet to receive any complaints that I've read.

Still, I admit that this system is not entirely perfect. For example, the wizard Isgarren came to my forge long ago seeking special compounds that I imagine were used for some magical purpose or another. I heard of this after the fact, and was most curious what one of his stature might want to get out of my collection! But upon closer investigation, I realized with a hint of despair that there was no record of what exactly Isgarren tossed into my forge, nor what he received in return, as the skritt are rather poor at maintaining proper documentation.

Also, their handwriting is quite terrible.

This has resulted in a much more robust plan to eventually implement a system that will record all of the items entering and exiting the forge. We've yet to put the plan into action, of course, as I like to give myself lots of time to stew over new ideas for the Mystic Forge operation before putting them in place. It's been a while, admittedly, but great ideas take time to perfect, and I have a lot of great ideas.

I maintain hope that someday that curious wizard will return with need of my services. Should the situation arise, I plan to inquire at length about the nature of his work and just where he has been all this time. But, until then, all I can do is have Miyani keep an ear to the ground. It has been a very long time since Isgarren has been seen or heard from, so I have my concerns.
